description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by whether they are “Targeted” (orange) or “Untargeted” (blue), as defined in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis indicates the “Number of datasets,” scaled from 0 to 160 in increments of 20. Each year is represented by a stacked bar, with the blue “Untargeted” portion at the bottom and the orange “Targeted” portion on top. In early years (2012–2015), dataset counts are very low, mostly under 5, with only one or two datasets per year. From 2016 onward, there is a clear upward trend: 2016 has ~12 total datasets (mostly targeted), 2017 has ~28 (14 targeted, 14 untargeted), 2018 has ~48 (20 targeted, 28 untargeted), 2019 has ~66 (52 targeted, 14 untargeted), 2020 has ~132 (48 targeted, 84 untargeted), and 2021 peaks at ~160 (66 targeted, 94 untargeted). In 2022, the total drops to ~38 (28 targeted, 10 untargeted). The chart visually emphasizes the rapid growth in dataset creation, particularly in 2020 and 2021, and shows that while “Targeted” datasets dominate in earlier growth phases, “Untargeted” datasets become more numerous in later years — especially in 2020 and 2021 — before declining in 2022.
